metadata.balance_sheet_source: CCLFX Annual Report, year ended March 31 2025
metadata.flow_data_source: Bloomberg / Robert A. Stanger & Co., data through March 23 2026
metadata.description: Four scenarios spanning historical growth, current tide-turning reality, and two stress cases. All use the same calibrated FY2025 balance sheet starting point.

scenarios._comment: Zero-net-flow baseline: calibrated balance sheet, subscriptions equal redemptions. Appropriate for testing distribution coverage in a stable-inflow environment.
scenarios.name: Calibrated Baseline

scenarios._comment: Bloomberg data (Q1 2026): redemptions ~8% of NAV vs. subscriptions ~5.5%. Net outflows of ~2.5% per quarter represent the first sustained period of net redemptions in fund history. Credit environment held constant — this isolates the pure flow-inversion effect.
scenarios.name: Tide Turning (Current)

scenarios._comment: Moderate credit stress analogous to a shallow recession: defaults 4%, LGD 45%, yield compression 60bp, modest net outflows. Distribution coverage under pressure but fund remains solvent. Reference: 2015-16 US oil & gas stress cycle.
scenarios.name: Mild Stress

scenarios._comment: Severe downturn analogous to 2008-09 GFC: defaults 10%, LGD 55%, portfolio yield compressed by 160bp, zero new subscriptions, redemptions at 10% per quarter as investors flee the asset class. PIK spikes as borrowers defer cash pay. Tests the fund's ability to service senior notes and the revolving facility under maximum stress.
scenarios.name: Severe Stress (2009-analog)
